messages:
lia: heads up — LAX POP p95 jumped from ~45ms to ~420ms starting ~18:02 UTC. Affects hosted and a few dedicated lanes. :eyes:

sam: saw it too, alerted on call. Any config rollouts?

lia: no deploys at that window from infra dashboard. metrics: token latency and tail both spiked, throughput steady-ish but more retries.

marta: I'm seeing a lot of IP fragmentation/errors from one upstream provider on the LAX eBGP path in network logs. MTU-related icmp frag-needed spikes around the same time.

jin: traceroute from an affected host -> showed a hop with consistent 1500->1200 path MTU mismatch. attaching mtr sample: ```
# mtr -c 20 -r 10.0.3.45
Host           Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
1. 10.0.3.1      0.0%    20    0.5   0.6   0.3   2.1   0.4
2. 198.51.100.1  0.0%    20   12.2  13.5  11.9  22.3   2.5
3. 203.0.113.5   0.0%    20   35.9  40.2  34.0  78.1  12.1
4. 198.51.101.7 10.0%    20  350.1 398.3 345.0 990.2 210.0
```

sam: ok that explains packet drops, but why is kv-cache thrashing mentioned in traces?

lia: runtime sidecar logs show increased KV cache miss ratio and then fallback to reconstructing prefixes—more CPU and larger kernels being chosen. Looks like fragmentation is causing lots of small retransmits so requests land later and kernel selector oscillates.

patrick: can you paste the profiling snippet?

lia: perf top snippet from a hot host: ```
  23.1%  runtime        [kernel]  tcp_recvmsg
  12.4%  runtime        libinference.so   kernel_selector::select_optimal
  8.9%   runtime        libbatching.so    batching::heuristic::evaluate
  6.7%   runtime        [kernel]  memcpy
  4.1%   runtime        libkvcache.so     kvcache::lookup
```

marta: so network fragmentation -> higher per-request latency -> more concurrent inflight batches for same requests -> batch heuristic upsizes to larger kernel paths -> CPU goes up -> qps per core drops -> latency tails blow up. Circular.

sam: agree. Immediate mitigations?

jin: I pushed a temporary routing preference to use private peering for LAX->AZ provider on the affected PoP. Also bumped NGINX proxy keepalive and lowered max_chunk_size to avoid sending large frames that trigger fragmentation.

lia: on runtime I toggled kvcache eviction to be more aggressive for LAX zone (ttl 30s -> 10s) to reduce stale large-prefetch pressure, and forced kernel-selector to prefer small-kernel path for <=512 tokens for the next 10m.

patrick: any observable impact?

deploy-bot: config-change:routing/lax-peering-prefer (by jin) at 18:24Z
deploy-bot: config-change:runtime/lax-kv-ttl (by lia) at 18:27Z

marta: after the peering flip latency p95 dropped to ~80-90ms within 3m. kv-cache miss rate still elevated but falling.

lia: after forcing small-kernel preference, CPU per host dropped ~22% and kernel-selection churn decreased. p99 still not fully recovered but trending down.

sam: good job. followups: 1) engage provider on MTU mismatch and ask for MTU alignment/ICMP handling 2) add MTU alarms and passive PMTU tracking 3) make kernel-selector less reactive to short-lived latency spikes (smoothing window) 4) add a routing fallback to peering earlier in policy.

patrick: also add a quick eval to see quality impact of small-kernel preference on long prompts — we need to ensure no regression. Lia, can you queue that?

lia: queued a small eval run against our regression set, tag lax-mtu-incident-180512. will share results in #eng-runtime with timings and token-level diffs.

marta: opened ticket with provider and included mtr + icmp dump. ref: TKT-3894. provider acknowledged and said they'll investigate path config, might take 24-48h.

jin: rolling back the forced small-kernel preference in 30m if eval looks clean. removing aggressive kv-ttl once provider confirms fix.

sam: add postmortem after we stabilize, include timeline, root cause (provider MTU handling) and mitigations implemented. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
